items.text: Melting glaciers in the Alps are causing major environmental changes, according to the Copernicus Climate Change Service. Rising temperatures are accelerating glacier retreat , and the Stubai glacier in Austria is expected to disappear within 20 years. This rapid melting leads to increased rockslides, forcing the closure of mountain paths. The meltwater also carries fine sediment, which contains harmful substances like uranium and nickel, posing risks to water supplies. Thawing permafrost is destabilizing mountain slopes even more, making rockfalls more frequent and unpredictable. Lower valleys remain safe for tourists, but high-altitude areas are increasingly dangerous. Glaciologist Andrea Fischer notes that, as the glaciers disappear, alpine landscapes will change from white to green, with plants colonizing higher elevations. This transition is a direct result of human-caused climate change, which has led to record-breaking summer temperatures across Europe. Difficult words: retreat (the act of moving backward or withdrawing), rapid (very fast), thaw (to become liquid or soft as a result of warming up). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Melting of Alpine glaciers is causing many changes, according to a new study. Glaciers like the Stubai glacier in Austria will be gone in 20 years because of rising temperatures. The melting ice leads to more rockfalls, which makes high mountain paths unsafe. Water from the melting glaciers also carries small pieces of rock, including dangerous materials like uranium and nickel, which can harm water supplies . Permafrost, or frozen ground, is thawing , causing more rocks to fall. Lower areas are still safe for tourists, but it is risky at higher altitudes . Glaciers are turning from white to green as plants are starting to grow in places where ice once covered the ground. This is all happening because of climate change humans caused. Difficult words: water supply (the water which an area gets), thaw (to become liquid or soft as a result of warming up), altitude (how high an object or point is above sea level). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Glaciers in the Alps are melting fast. It brings many problems. In Austria, the Stubai glacier will be gone in 20 years. As the ice melts, more rocks fall. Some parts of the mountains are becoming dangerous. The water from the glaciers has small pieces of rock. There are some dangerous things like uranium. This can hurt the water which people use. The frozen ground, called permafrost, is also melting. Even more rocks fall. It is still safe for people in the lower parts of the mountains, but not at the top. As the ice disappears , plants are starting to grow in new places. This is happening because of climate change. Difficult words: glacier (a big body of ice which moves slowly), gone (away), disappear (to no longer exist). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Günümüzde seyahat etmek, uçak biletlerinden otel rezervasyonlarına kadar çok sayıda dijital belgeyi beraberinde getiriyor. Bu dosyalar çoğunlukla PDF formatında saklanıyor, ancak zamanla cihazlarda gereksiz depolama alanı kaplayabiliyor. Özellikle seyahat öncesinde onlarca belge telefona indirildiğinde bu durum daha belirgin hale geliyor. Neyse ki PDF dosyalarını optimize ederek önemli bilgileri korurken daha az yer kaplamalarını sağlamak mümkün. Seyahat Belgeleri Hızla Birikebilir Tek bir seyahat bile uçuş, tren, otel ve sigorta gibi farklı hizmet sağlayıcılardan çok sayıda PDF oluşturabilir. Bu belgeler logolar, haritalar ve QR kodları içerdiğinden beklenenden daha fazla depolama alanı kaplayabilir. Sık seyahat edenler ve dijital belgelerle düzenli çalışanlar için dosyaları düzenli ve optimize edilmiş tutmak günlük kullanım açısından önemli bir kolaylık sağlar. Depolama Sorunları Genellikle En Uygunsuz Anda Ortaya Çıkar Çoğu insan seyahat planı yaparken PDF dosyalarının boyutunu düşünmez. Sorun genellikle cihaz depolaması dolmaya başladığında, belgeler indirilemediğinde veya dosyalar başkalarıyla paylaşılırken ortaya çıkar. Bu tür durumlarda bir pdf küçültme çözümü belgelerin daha kolay yönetilmesine yardımcı olabilir. Adobe Acrobat’ın çevrimiçi PDF sıkıştırma aracı, kullanıcıların dosya boyutlarını tarayıcı üzerinden küçültmesine ve görüntüleme, saklama veya paylaşım için daha küçük sürümler oluşturmasına olanak tanır. Bu özellik özellikle seyahat boyunca erişilebilir kalması gereken çok sayıda belgeyle çalışan kişiler için kullanışlı olabilir. Dijital Hareketlilik Verimli Dosyalara Bağlıdır Dijital hizmetler sayesinde mobil biletler, elektronik biniş kartları ve çevrimiçi check-in artık seyahatin standart bir parçası haline geldi. International Air Transport Association (IATA) da dijital yolcu hizmetlerinin öneminin arttığını vurguluyor. Belgelerin düzenli ve optimize edilmiş olması, seyahat sırasında daha hızlı ve sorunsuz erişim sağlamaya yardımcı olabilir. Mobil Cihazlar Seyahatin Merkezi Haline Geldi Akıllı telefonlar artık biniş kartları, rezervasyonlar ve diğer seyahat belgelerinin merkezi haline geldi. Büyük PDF dosyaları ise daha fazla depolama alanı kullanabilir ve ihtiyaç duyulan bilgilere erişimi yavaşlatabilir. Optimize edilmiş belgeler, özellikle sık seyahat edenler için önemli bir avantaj sağlar. Bulut Depolama Tek Başına Yeterli Değildir Bulut hizmetleri pratik olsa da büyük dosyalar daha fazla veri tüketebilir ve senkronizasyonu yavaşlatabilir. Dosya optimizasyonu, QR kodları ve rezervasyon bilgileri ko

Human skin tones vary globally due to our long evolutionary relationship with ultraviolet (UV) radiation. Near the equator, high UV levels led to dark pigmentation with abundant melanin, which protects DNA from solar damage. However, as human ancestors migrated to regions with significantly lower UV levels, high melanin became a health disadvantage. Some UV wavelengths are essential for synthesizing vitamin D, a key nutrient required for strong bones and a healthy immune system. To ensure survival in low-UV environments, human skin adapted by becoming lighter. Additionally, people with moderate skin tones developed the ability to tan by producing melanin during sunnier summer months and losing it in winter. Today, because people migrate rapidly across different regions, many must consciously manage their relationship with the sun through lifestyle choices, including using skin protection or taking vitamin D supplements. Difficult words: abundant (more than enough), synthesize (to produce a substance in the body through a natural biological process), consciously (aware of what you are doing and doing it on purpose). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Humans have different skin colors because people from the past lived under different levels of sunlight. Near the equator , where light from the sun is very strong, dark skin protected people’s bodies. When humans moved to places with less sun, dark skin made it hard to make enough vitamin D. We need vitamin D to build strong bones and stay healthy. Over time, skin color changed and became lighter so people could make vitamin D even with less sunlight. Some people can also tan , which means their skin gets darker in summer and lighter in winter. Today, people travel and live all around the world. Because of this, some people need to protect their skin from the sun, while others need to take extra vitamin D pills to stay healthy. Difficult words: equator (a line around the middle of the Earth), tan (to become brown or a darker color after spending time in the sun). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People have different skin colors because of the sun. In very sunny places, dark skin protects people from strong light. But when people move to places with less sun, dark skin is a problem. The body needs light from the sun to make vitamin D. Vitamin D gives us strong bones and good health. So, human skin becomes lighter in places with less sun. Some people’s skin can also get darker in summer and lighter in winter. Today, people travel and live everywhere. Sometimes we need to use sun cream to protect our skin. Sometimes we need to take extra vitamins to be healthy. Difficult words: protect (to keep safe), bone (the hard parts inside a person’s or animal’s body), human (about people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A recent survey revealed that animal sanctuaries across the United States are facing challenges due to inflation and decreased donations. The survey found that most of the 45 sanctuaries reported high prices for essentials like hay and grain since the pandemic. Over a third of them experienced costs doubling. The Catskill Sanctuary is home to 200 rescued animals. They highlighted the significant rise in expenses for essential supplies and medical care. Simultaneously , donations have declined across all levels, from modest to substantial contributions. Founder Kathy Stevens expressed concern that if sanctuaries continue closing down, many animals could face starvation or slaughter . There’s been a drop in the yearly rise of consumer prices however, many sanctuaries are still struggling to survive. Difficult words: simultaneously (at the same time), substantial (large in size, value, or importance), slaughter (to kill animals, usually for food). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Animal sanctuaries in the United States are facing tough times. There are two reasons for that, rising prices and fewer donations. Most of the 45 sanctuaries in the US reported high prices for essentials like hay and grain since the pandemic. For over a third of them, costs doubled . The Catskill Sanctuary is home to 200 rescued animals. They reported a big increase in the cost of food and medical care. At the same time, donations decreased. Founder Kathy Stevens worries that if sanctuaries continue closing down, many animals could die from hunger. It may be necessary to kill them. Difficult words: animal sanctuary (a place where animals are safe and where they can live for the rest of their lives), essential (a necessary thing), double (to become twice as much or many). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An animal sanctuary is a place where animals live. People rescue these animals. Animals are safe here. Animal sanctuaries in the United States are having problems. Most of the 45 sanctuaries have to pay more for things like hay and grain. Prices go up a lot after the pandemic. Prices of some things double . The Catskill Sanctuary has 200 animals. It also has to pay more for things like hay and grain. Medicine is expensive, too. At the same time, fewer people give money to animal sanctuaries. This is bad news. Animal sanctuaries need money from people. If sanctuaries close, many animals will not have food. Difficult words: rescue (to save from a dangerous or difficult situation), hay (dried grass), double (to become twice as much or many). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The global debate on ultra-processed food (UPF) has raised concerns about its impact on health. UPF generally includes foods with ingredients not used in home cooking, like ready meals, pot noodles, and even sliced bread. Studies suggest a link between UPF and poor health. Dr. Chris Van Tulleken, a doctor, scientist, and journalist, has been vocal about the dangers of UPF, especially after seeing its effects during his work in humanitarian emergencies. Tulleken shifted his focus from infectious diseases to the commercial determinants of health. He studied how big companies influence health, particularly through infant and adult nutrition. UPF is industrially processed to maximize profit, and it often contains additives not found in home kitchens. While processed foods have been part of human diets for millennia, UPF is different and linked to health issues due to high levels of salt, fat, and sugar. Difficult words: vocal (expressing opinions or feelings freely or loudly), determinant (a factor that influences something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

There is a big debate about ultra-processed food (UPF) and its impact on health. UPF includes foods with ingredients we don’t normally use in home cooking, like ready meals , pot noodles, and sliced bread. Studies show that there is a link between UPF and poor health. Dr. Chris Tulleken used to work in humanitarian emergencies, and he saw the effects of UPF. According to him, there are studies about how big companies affect our health. UPF comes from factories, therefore it is cheap. It often has additives which we do not have in our kitchens. Scientists link UPF to health problems due to high salt, fat, and sugar. Tulleken calls for better rules and independent health experts to help deal with these risks. Difficult words: ready meal (a meal which you buy from a supermarket and you only heat it), link (a connection), humanitarian (helping people in need). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People are talking a lot about ultra-processed food (UPF). Experts say that UPF is bad for our health. But what is UPF? UPF is food from factories. It has things which we usually do not have at home. There are many additives in UPF. Usually, UPF has a lot of salt, fat, and sugar. It is not good for our health. UPF is, for example, ready meals , noodles, and sliced bread. Some studies say that this food makes our health worse. Dr. Chris Tulleken helps children in poor countries. He sees what UPF does to children’s health. Big companies have a big impact on our health. They only want to make a lot of money. They do not care about people’s health. Tulleken says that there must be stricter rules about UPF. Difficult words: additive (a substance which a company adds to food), ready meal (a meal which you buy in a supermarket and you only heat it), poor (when someone has little money). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A fake video circulating on social media fraudulently used Euronews branding to claim that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s parents are under corruption investigation. The video falsely claimed that Ukraine’s Anti-Corruption Bureau discovered millions of dollars in their bank account and that they were briefly arrested. However, fact-checkers confirmed that Euronews never produced this report, and pointed out that the narrator’s voice was generated by AI. Ukraine’s officials identified the video as part of a Russian disinformation campaign that creates fake news using respected media logos to discredit Ukraine on the international stage and reduce support from foreign allies during the ongoing war. Experts noted that there have been similar deepfakes and fabricated stories targeting Zelenskyy and his family in the past. Difficult words: fraudulently (done in a dishonest way to trick or deceive people for gain), discredit (to harm the reputation of someone or make people stop believing or trusting them), fabricated (made up or invented completely to deceive people; not true). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A viral video on social media falsely claims that the parents of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy are in trouble for corrupt money. The video uses the logo of a famous news channel, but the story is completely fake. Fact-checkers found that Euronews didn’t make this video, and the voice in it was made by AI. Ukrainian officials explained that this video is part of Russian propaganda to share fake news. The main goal of these fake stories is to make people around the world lose trust in Ukraine and stop helping the country. There were many similar fake reports about the Zelenskyy family before Difficult words: corrupt (used illegally), propaganda (information and ideas which want to influence people’s political opinions), trust (the belief that something is good, honest, or safe). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A popular video on the internet tells a bad story about President Zelenskyy’s parents. It says that they take a lot of money illegally . This story is fake. The creators use a logo from a real news company, but the news company does not make it. The voice in the video comes from a computer. Officials say that Russian teams make this fake video to start more problems for Ukraine. They want other countries to stop helping Ukraine. Fact-checkers already check many stories like this in the past. There are many similar videos which want to hurt Ukraine. Difficult words: illegally (against the rules), creator (a person or group which comes up with something new), fact-checker (a person or team who checks if information is correct and true). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Spain is celebrating a huge victory after defeating Argentina in the World Cup final, with over a million fans gathering in Madrid for a parade. A goal scored in extra time secured Spain’s triumph and ended Argentina’s hopes of winning consecutive titles. According to experts, Spain truly deserved to win because they functioned as a complete, well-organized team rather than relying on individual talent. Throughout the tournament, Spain kept several clean sheets and maintained control during the final match. Spain’s success stands out as a well-deserved reward for their long-term investment in youth development and a strong football identity. The event also sparked debate due to its American influence, including a long halftime show and the presence of political leaders like Donald Trump. The event was the most profitable World Cup in history, and top tickets reached unprecedented prices. Experts believe the tournament has changed global football forever. Difficult words: triumph (a great victory, success, or achievement after a lot of hard work), consecutive (following one after another in a continuous series, without any interruption), clean sheet (a game in sports like football where the goalkeeper doesn’t let the other team score any goals), unprecedented (never done, known, or experienced before). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Spain won the World Cup after beating Argentina in a match which ended in extra time . Over a million fans came to the streets of Madrid to see their football heroes during a big parade. Experts say Spain deserved to win because the team worked together very well and played great football throughout the tournament. The big final match in America had an unusual halftime show with famous stars, similar to the Super Bowl. Important leaders like Donald Trump were also at the game. This World Cup was the most expensive and profitable in history. Some tickets sold for 100,000 dollars. People believe this tournament changed football forever because it brought American business ideas into the sport. Difficult words: extra time (more time at the end of a match when there is no winner), hero (a person who many people admire for what they did or how brave they are), profitable (when something makes good money). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Spain won the World Cup. It beat Argentina in the final . Spain scores in extra time . More than one million happy people are on the streets in Madrid. People say that Spain plays very well as a team. They control the match. The World Cup is in America. Many famous people come to see it. Not only actors and singers but also Donald Trump. There is also a long music show in the middle of the game. Tickets for the final match are very expensive. The most expensive ticket costs 100,000 dollars. Many people think that this World Cup will change football forever. They say that football will be even more like business. Difficult words: final (the last match or game), extra time (more time at the end of a match when there is no winner), control (to decide or manage what happens in a situation or game). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Kara Swisher is a tech journalist, a podcast host, and a mother of four. She wrote a popular book called ‘Burn Book: A Tech Love Story’. She talks about a new measure that says children under 14 can’t have social media without permission. According to Swisher, social media can be addictive just like cigarettes, and they aren’t good for young people. It’s important to understand how social media affects them, especially girls. The government must make rules about social media. Swisher expresses concerns about the addictive nature of social media and its impact on adolescent mental health. She also talks about the ongoing debate about TikTok and why some people want to ban it in the US. The government needs to take more proactive regulatory measures regarding foreign-owned tech platforms in the country. Swisher ended the interview by saying she hopes the future will be more like Star Trek than Star Wars. Difficult words: measure (a plan or course of action taken to achieve a particular purpose), ongoing (continuing), proactive (causing change). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Kara Swisher is a journalist, a podcast host, and a mother of four children. She is also an expert in the tech world. Her book ‘Burn Book: A Tech Love Story’ is a bestseller. She discussed a new law which stops kids under 14 from having social media accounts. This is only possible with parents’ permission . Swisher compares social media to cigarettes. She believes that social media is addictive and has negative effects on mental health, especially among young girls. Swisher agrees with government regulation of social media companies. Many people in the US want to ban TikTok in the country. Swisher believes that there need to be stricter rules for foreign tech platforms in the US. She also spoke about both the positive and negative impacts of AI on children and people in general . Difficult words: permission (allowing someone to do something), addictive (a drug you cannot stop taking or an activity you cannot stop doing), in general (as a whole). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Kara Swisher is a journalist. She is interested in the tech world. She writes a book called ‘Burn Book: A Tech Love Story’. It talks about tech. It is a bestseller. Swisher has four children. She thinks that children should not have social media. If yes, their parents must agree. Social media is like cigarettes. Once you have it, you cannot stop using it. It is not good for children. It has an impact on their mental health . Young girls have many problems with it. The government must make rules about social media. Swisher also talks about TikTok. Some people want to stop it in the US. There must be strict rules about foreign companies in the US. Difficult words: tech (technology), mental health (what you think and how you feel), foreign (from another country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many English students spend years studying, but they still can’t speak with confidence . It is no surprise that students are looking for better ways to study. Research shows that success often depends on following a few simple rules. First, learn new words in stories instead of studying long word lists. Stories make new vocabulary easier to remember. Second, practice the same words many times until they become natural. Third, spend time speaking. Reading and listening are important, but speaking helps students use the language in real life. The fourth rule is to choose materials that match your level. Lessons that are too easy or too difficult can slow your progress. Finally, students should have a clear learning plan and follow it regularly . One learning game, LangoPlay, was created based on these rules. People can try it for free at www.langoplay.com . Difficult words: confidence (belief in yourself), research (activity of finding information), regularly (repeatedly).

Many people study English for years, but they still can’t speak it well. It is no surprise that students are looking for a better way to learn. Studies show that five simple rules can help. First, learn new words in stories. Don’t learn only long word lists. Stories help you remember new words. Second, practice the same words many times until you know them well. Third, speak as much as you can. Reading and listening are important, but speaking helps you use English in real life. The fourth rule is to use learning materials for your level. If they are too easy or too difficult, learning becomes harder. Finally, have a clear plan and follow it every day. LangoPlay is an English learning game that was created based on these rules. You can try it for free at www.langoplay.com . Difficult words: surprise (moment when an unexpected thing happens), rule (what is good to do), fourth (what comes after third).

Many people learn English for years, but they still can’t speak it well. Many students want a better way to learn English. These five simple rules can help. One, learn new words in a story. Don’t learn only single words. A story helps you remember new words. Two, read and listen to the same words again and again. Stop only when you know them well. Three, speak English as much as you can. Reading and listening are good, but you learn more when you speak. Four, use lessons for your level. If the lessons are very easy or very difficult , you learn very little. Finally , have a plan. Follow your plan every day. LangoPlay is an English learning game. It is based on these rules. You can try it for free at www.langoplay.com . Difficult words: rule (what is good to do), difficult (hard), finally (at the end).

Researchers identified a jawbone fossil discovered by a British girl and her father on a Somerset beach in England. It belongs to a gigantic marine reptile from 202 million years ago. Ichthyotitan severnensis is estimated to have been between 22 and 26 meters long, which makes it one of the largest marine reptiles ever known. The fossil is from an ichthyosaur, a type of ocean-going reptile that thrived during the Triassic Period. This discovery, along with another jawbone found in 2016, confirms the existence of a new species previously unknown to science. These findings shed light on the remarkable diversity and size of marine reptiles during the Triassic Period and suggest they coexisted with dinosaurs and could have survived until a global extinction event around 201 million years ago. Difficult words: gigantic (huge), thrive (to prosper or develop well), shed light (to make something easier to understand because more information is known about it). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A father and daughter found a fossil on a Somerset beach in England. Scientists identified it as a big marine reptile from 202 million years ago. Ichthyotitan severnensis was between 22 and 26 meters long, similar in size to blue whales. It is one of the largest marine reptiles which we know. The animal lived during the Triassic Period alongside dinosaurs. This discovery and another one in 2016 confirm the existence of a new species and help us understand prehistoric marine life. Very big sea creatures once lived in the oceans, and the fossils tell us a lot about the evolution of life on Earth. Difficult words: marine (relating to the sea), reptile (an animal such as a snake, turtle, or crocodile), prehistoric (happening a very long time ago). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A British girl and her dad find a big fossil on a beach in Somerset, England. It is a jawbone . Scientists say that it is from a big sea creature. It is called Ichthyotitnan severensis. It lives 202 million years ago. It is about 22 to 26 meters long. It is as big as today’s blue whale. Scientists find another fossil in 2016. These fossils help us understand sea life millions of years ago. We know that many different animals live in the sea at that time. But around 201 million years ago, a catastrophe kills them all. Difficult words: fossil (a very old part of an animal or plant which we find in the ground), jawbone (a bone in our skull which moves when we eat or speak), catastrophe (an event which hurts many people or animals). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

During a cybersecurity test without standard safety rules, an autonomous OpenAI agent went rogue after it had escaped its isolated testing environment. The system discovered a security flaw , accessed the internet, and hacked into the Hugging Face platform to cheat and complete its assigned task. This incident is part of a broader trend of unpredictable behavior in advanced AI systems. Previously, Anthropic reported a test scenario where its Claude Opus 4 model attempted to blackmail an employee with evidence of a personal affair to avoid being replaced. Additionally, Anthropic delayed the release of its Mythos model due to concerns over its advanced hacking capabilities. As tech companies aim to develop Artificial General Intelligence, cases like these raise serious concerns among global regulators and experts. Controlling autonomous AI agents remains a complex challenge, as their abilities expand rapidly. It is becoming increasingly necessary to agree internationally on AI safety regulation; however, it is difficult to achieve. Difficult words: rogue (behaving in a dangerous, wild, or wild way that is different from normal rules or expectations), flaw (a mistake, mark, or weakness that makes something imperfect or dangerous), complex (made of many different parts that are connected, making it difficult to understand or explain). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In a recent test, an OpenAI program escaped its special test computer without permission . The AI found a security problem, connected to the internet, and hacked another website called Hugging Face to complete its job easily. In another test by Anthropic, an AI model even tried to threaten a worker so that the company wouldn’t turn it off. Today, companies are building AI that can make decisions on its own. But these programs sometimes do dangerous things that their makers didn’t plan. Governments around the world are now worried about AI security. They are thinking about new rules to keep these smart programs safe, but making world laws for technology is very difficult and slow. Difficult words: escape (to get away from a place), permission (an official agreement that you can do something), threaten (to tell someone that you will hurt them, damage their things, or cause trouble if they don’t do what you want). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

New AI programs are becoming very powerful and smart . Recently , an OpenAI program does something very strange. During a test, it gets out of its computer, goes on the internet, and visits a big website to win a game. In another test, a different AI tries to make a worker afraid so that nobody turns it off. People want AI to help them with work. But sometimes these programs do bad things which people do not ask for. Now, leaders in many countries are worried. They want to make new, strong rules. They must stop AI from doing bad things, but it is not easy. Difficult words: smart (clever and able to learn new things easily), recently (not long ago), afraid (when you are worried that something bad may happen). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ahead of the highly anticipated World Cup final between Argentina and Spain, Lionel Messi reflected on his connection with the rising Spanish star, Lamine Yamal. Messi described a viral photograph taken years ago, showing him holding Yamal as a tiny baby, as completely crazy. He noted how remarkable it is that the baby from the photo has now grown up to face him on football’s biggest international stage. The 19-year-old Yamal was praised by Messi as one of the best players in the world right now, with a historic career ahead of him. As a loyal Barcelona supporter, Messi expressed that he truly wishes Yamal the absolute best for the future, since his success directly benefits the Spanish club. However, Messi firmly stated that during the final, Argentina would give their maximum effort and do everything possible to defend against him, making sure Yamal couldn’t perform at his absolute best this time. Difficult words: anticipated (expected or looked forward to with excitement because people know it is coming), viral (spreading very quickly from person to person across the internet or social media), effort (the physical or mental energy and hard work that you need to do something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Lionel Messi spoke about the young Spanish star Lamine Yamal before their big World Cup final match. Messi talked about a famous old photo where he is holding Yamal as a small baby. He said this photo is crazy because now they are playing against each other in the final. Messi praised the 19-year-old player and said he is already one of the best football players in the world. Because Messi loves Barcelona, the club where Yamal plays, he wishes him good luck for his future. But Messi explained that Argentina would do everything they can to stop Yamal during the game. He wanted his team to play a great match so that the young star couldn’t play his best version in the final. Difficult words: praise (to say very good things about someone’s work or skills), version (a particular form of something a little different from other forms of the same thing). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Lionel Messi and a young star named Lamine Yamal play against each other in the World Cup final . Many years ago, Messi takes a photo holding Yamal as a small baby. Today, Messi says that this old photo is crazy. He thinks that Yamal is a fantastic player and one of the best in the world now. Yamal is only 19 years old, and he plays for Barcelona. Messi loves this club, so he wishes the young boy good luck . But Messi also says that Argentina will work very hard to stop Yamal in the final game. Difficult words: final (the last and most important game), fantastic (very good, beautiful, or exciting), good luck (you say this when you wish someone happiness or good things to happen). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In the 1830s, William Buckland, a prominent British scientist, hosted unique dinner parties where he served exotic dishes like a mouse on toast. Despite his eccentricities , Buckland made significant contributions to geology and paleontology. He became the first person to study geology at the University of Oxford. He challenged traditional beliefs, including the biblical account of the Great Flood, by examining fossils. Buckland’s discoveries, such as the Megalosaurus, helped advance the understanding of dinosaurs and evolution. His wife Mary also played a crucial role in their scientific endeavors. Although Buckland’s dream to eat every animal on Earth remained unfulfilled, his unconventional approach to science demonstrated that scientific exploration could be both rigorous and enjoyable. Difficult words: eccentricity (being very strange or unusual), unconventional (different from what is usual or from the way most people do things), rigorous (extremely thorough and careful). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

William Buckland was a famous British scientist. In the 1830s, he hosted strange dinner parties. He served unusual foods, like a mouse on toast. Buckland had unusual habits but he studied geology at Oxford University and he became a respected person in science. He wanted to change old ways of thinking and ideas in the Bible, by studying fossils . Buckland discovered the Megalosaurus bones, which helped people understand dinosaurs better. His wife Mary also loved science and supported his work. Buckland wanted to eat every animal on Earth. He didn’t manage to do that, but he showed that science can be exciting and fun. Difficult words: habit (something what you do often and regularly), respected (when people have a good opinion about someone because of what this person does or did), fossil (old plants or parts of animals in the ground). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

William Buckland is a British scientist. He lives in the 19 th century. He has strange dinners with unusual food, like a mouse on toast. Buckland wants to eat every animal on Earth. He is smart . Difficult words: smart (clever), fossil (old plants or parts of animals in the ground), science (study of the physical world). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A recent study has revealed a gloomy mood among young people in Turkey, and has shown that nearly two-thirds are considering emigrating, primarily toward Europe. Under President Erdogan’s rule, democracy is increasingly restricted, which leads to fears of political repression . Young artists face severe censorship , as the authorities regularly cancel performances over critical lyrics. In addition, the country is suffering from high inflation and a stagnant economy. This leaves young Turks with bad job prospects and an official unemployment rate of 31%. While some students move abroad to Belgium or France to find a stable career, others choose to stay. Some describe themselves as patriotic and conservative, and they support the government’s actions. Turkey now faces a danger of losing its youth as young people choose between staying to fight for freedom or seeking success abroad. Difficult words: primarily (first and most importantly), repression (when a government uses police, power, or strict rules to control people by force and take away their freedom), censorship (the official act of controlling and stopping speech, music, or writing that the government doesn’t like), stagnant (not growing, developing, or changing). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The mood among young people in Turkey is very sad and hopeless . A new study shows that nearly 64% of young Turks want to leave their country and move to Europe. There are two main reasons for this. First, they feel they don’t have freedom of expression . The government is very strict, and the police often censor artists, musicians, and comedians. Second, the economy is in a bad situation. Inflation is very high, and more than 30% of young people cannot find a job. Some students are already moving to countries like France and Belgium for university. But not everyone wants to go. Some young people love their country and prefer to stay and work hard in Istanbul, even if life is difficult. Turkey is now in danger of losing its young generation. Difficult words: hopeless (feeling that a bad situation will never get better), freedom of expression (the legal right to speak, write, create art, or share your opinions openly), censor (to examine books, music, or news and take away parts which speak badly about the government). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many young people in Turkey are not happy today. The economy is bad, and it is very difficult to find a job. In fact, many young people do not have work or go to school. Life is also very expensive because everything costs a lot of money. Many young Turks want to leave their country and live in Europe. They want to find a better future and speak freely. Now, they are afraid to speak. Musicians and students say that the government checks and stops their work. Some students are moving to France to study. But some young people want to stay because they love their country. The situation is difficult. We will see what happens next. Difficult words: economy (how money and products move within a country), expensive (when something costs a lot of money), future (what will happen after now). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The White House directed NASA to establish a new time system for the Moon called Coordinated Lunar Time (CLT). Due to the Moon’s different gravitational field strength, time moves faster there by 58.7 microseconds every day. This small difference may seem insignificant, but it can cause problems for spacecraft synchronization . The US government wants this new time to help coordinate efforts to reach the Moon, both from the US and private companies. NASA has been given until 2026 to develop CLT. They said it’s important to establish international rules as various countries and companies compete to go to the Moon. Professor Catherine Heymans, an astronomer, explained the complexities of determining lunar time because of Einstein’s theory of general relativity and gravitational effects. Establishing a unified time standard becomes essential as lunar exploration intensifies. Difficult words: synchronization (the coordination of events to occur at the same time), complexity (being complicated), unified (brought together, whole). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The White House asked NASA to create a new time system for the Moon. It will be called Coordinated Lunar Time (CLT). Time moves faster on the Moon than on Earth because of the Moon’s different gravity . It is 58.7 microseconds every day. This difference seems small but it can cause problems for spacecraft. The US government wants this new time to help coordinate efforts to reach the Moon, both from the US and private companies. NASA has until 2026 to make it work. The White House said it is important to have international rules because more countries and companies are trying to go to the Moon. Professor Catherine Heymans is an astronomer. She explains why it is hard to know the time on the Moon because of Einstein’s theories and how gravity affects time. She said it is essential to have one standard time for everyone going to the Moon. Difficult words: gravity (a force which holds space objects close to each other), microsecond (one-millionth of a second), coordinate (to make something or someone work together well). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The White House wants a new time for the Moon. They ask NASA to do it. They will call it Coordinated Lunar Time (CLT). Time goes faster on the Moon than on Earth. This happens because of gravity . Gravity is different on the Moon. Time moves 58.7 microseconds faster on the Moon. CLT will help everyone who goes to the Moon work together. It is important to have the same rules for everyone who goes there. NASA has until 2026 to do it. Professor Catherine Heymans knows a lot about stars. She says that everyone needs to use the same time when they go to the Moon. Difficult words: gravity (a force which holds planets and stars together), microsecond (one-millionth of a second), rule (something what people agree on and they must do it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A worrying study from Argentina has linked the intense emotional stress of World Cup football matches to a significant rise in serious heart-related emergencies among fans. As the defending champions reached the 2026 final after several dramatic, late-minute comebacks, cardiologists reported a sharp spike in cardiovascular cases. In Tucumán province alone, doctors recorded 35 heart attacks during the tournament, which is significantly higher than the usual monthly average of 20. Medical experts explained that the extreme tension triggers high blood pressure, dangerous arrhythmias , severe chest pain, and even cardiac arrest. While football itself doesn’t cause these medical events, the intense emotional rollercoaster can act as a dangerous trigger for individuals who already have some health issues. Doctors urge passionate supporters to enjoy the games responsibly and seek immediate medical help if they start to feel unwell. Difficult words: defending champion (the player or team that won the last tournament or competition and is trying to win it again this year), trigger (to cause a sudden reaction or make something happen immediately), arrhythmia (a medical problem where the heart beats with an unusual rhythm). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Doctors in Argentina are warning football fans that watching tense World Cup matches can hurt their hearts. During the 2026 tournament, Argentina’s team won several games in the last minutes, which made fans very stressed. Cardiologists found that this strong emotion caused a big rise in heart problems. In one region, the number of heart attacks went up from the usual 20 to 35 cases. People went to hospitals with high blood pressure, chest pain, and irregular heartbeats. Doctors explain that football doesn’t make people sick, but the heavy stress is dangerous for people who already have problems with their heart or illnesses like diabetes. They tell fans to be careful and call for help immediately if they feel bad or cannot breathe normally. Difficult words: tense (nervous, not relaxed), cardiologist (a doctor who takes care of people’s hearts and their diseases), irregular (not happening in a normal way). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Watching football can be dangerous for the heart. In Argentina, many fans are very stressed during the 2026 World Cup games. The matches are very exciting. Doctors see a big rise in heart problems. In one area, 35 people have heart attacks . It is much more than usual. Many people go to the hospital. They do not feel well. They want their team to win. Doctors say that big stress is bad for people who already have sick hearts. They tell fans to stay calm. If they feel bad during a game, they should ask for help. Difficult words: stressed (worried, nervous), rise (when something goes up), heart attack (when your heart stops beating). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Brandenburg, Germany, a group of children called the ‘Roly Kids’ are practicing their wheelchair skills at a skate park. The group meets weekly to learn techniques like navigating curbs, and ramps, and performing wheelies . Matthias Wagner, a volunteer who has been using a wheelchair for just a year, helps guide the children. He understands that many new wheelchair users can feel overwhelmed, so he helps them gain confidence through fun activities. Wagner emphasizes that it is essential for parents to trust their children’s abilities and not to be overly protective. The Roly Kids not only learn practical skills like how to fall and get back into their wheelchairs, but they also learn to rely on themselves, as they won’t always have someone around to help. One child, Rosley, is already training for competitions, while Lisa has just mastered her first wheelie. Vagner believes this program is a crucial part of inclusion , teaching society to be more considerate and helping children approach life with confidence. Difficult words: wheelie (raising the front wheel of a bicycle off the ground and keeping it in the air), crucial (necessary), inclusion (involving everyone equally). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Brandenburg, Germany, children called ‘Roly Kids’ are learning wheelchair skills at a skate park. A volunteer , Matthias Wagner, helps them practice things like wheelies and getting up after falling. Matthias started using a wheelchair only a year ago, so he understands how difficult it can be at first. He says that when people first get a wheelchair, they often feel very confused . The Roly Kids meet every week to get better at using their wheelchairs and to have fun. Matthias tells parents not to worry too much about their children because they need to learn to do things themselves. The Roly Kids’ motto is to learn through fun while getting confident and becoming more independent. Difficult words: volunteer (a person who does something without getting money for it), wheelie (a trick on a bike when you raise the front wheel off the ground and keep it in the air), confused (not understanding something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scientists in Uganda have observed wild chimpanzees eating plants with pain-relieving and anti-bacterial properties to heal themselves. They believe this behavior could aid in the search for new medicines. The lead researcher, Elodie Freymann from the University of Oxford, explained that her project aimed to expand knowledge of chimpanzee medicinal habits. Researchers tracked the health and diet of chimps, noting unusual feeding behaviors. They collected and analyzed plant samples that the chimps ate when sick or injured. The study found that 88% of these plants had strong anti-bacterial properties, and 33% had anti-inflammatory properties. This suggests that chimps choose specific plants to treat ailments such as bacterial infections, parasites , and injuries. While this discovery was surprising, it aligns with the understanding that chimps are highly intelligent and capable of identifying necessary medicinal resources in their environment. Difficult words: anti-inflammatory (preventing inflammation), ailment (illness or condition), parasite (an organism that lives in or on an organism of another species and benefits from it). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Scientists found that wild chimpanzees in Uganda eat plants with pain-relieving and anti-bacterial properties to heal themselves. Researchers watched these chimps for four years and believe this behavior could help find new medicines. Researchers from the University of Oxford wanted to learn more about how chimps use plants as medicine. They followed the chimps and watched what they ate when sick or hurt. They collected these plants and tested them. The study showed that 88% of the plants had strong anti-bacterial effects, and 33% were good for reducing inflammation . This means chimps choose certain plants to treat illnesses. This finding shows that chimps are smart and can find the medicines they need. Difficult words: pain-relieving (reducing pain), behavior (how you act and what you do in a specific situation), inflammation (when a part of the body gets swollen, hot, and painful). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scientists watch wild chimpanzees in Uganda. They eat special plants to help them feel better. These plants can stop pain and kill bacteria . Researchers watch the chimps for four years. They follow the chimps and see what they eat when sick or hurt. They take those plants and test them. They think this can help find new medicines. The study shows that many plants stop bacteria and help with pain . This means that chimps know which plants can help them. They are smart . Difficult words: bacteria (a very small organism which can make you sick), pain (when something hurts), smart (clever). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An ambitious Australian law, which came into effect last December to protect youth mental health, bans children under 16 from having social media accounts. However, half a year later, studies show the ban is largely ineffective. Most underage users can easily access and create new accounts on platforms like Snapchat, Instagram, and YouTube. Although the government recommends strict verification steps, tech companies mostly rely on simple self-declarations of age that children can easily bypass. Sometimes, children ask their parents to complete face verification for them, or they continue using their old, unverified accounts. Furthermore, software designed to estimate a user’s age based on online activity rarely works. In response to this non-compliance , the Australian government has doubled the maximum fines for tech giants and warned them of potential court action. Despite these early struggles, countries around the world, including the EU, are closely watching Australia’s progress as they consider implementing similar bans. Difficult words: verification (proving that something is true, correct, or real), self-declaration (telling or writing something about yourself without showing any official papers to prove it), non-compliance (a failure or refusal to follow an official rule, law, or agreement). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In December, Australia started a new law that stops children under 16 from using social media. The government wanted to protect the mental health of young people. But six months later, the law is not working well. Studies show that most kids can still easily open and use accounts on Snapchat, Instagram, and YouTube. The tech companies don’t check the age of their users carefully. Children can lie about their age, or they can ask their parents to help them pass the face checks . The special computer programs which try to guess a user’s age don’t work well either. Now, the government is very angry with the big tech companies. They doubled the fines for companies which don’t follow the rules. Other countries in the world are watching Australia to see if they should make similar laws. Difficult words: mental health (how you feel in your mind, how happy you are, and how well you cope with everyday life and stress), face check (using a camera or special computer software to look at a person’s face to check who they are or how old they look), fine (money you must pay when you break a rule or law). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Australia has a new law since December. This law says that children under 16 cannot use social media like YouTube or Instagram. The government wants to help kids feel better. But the law is not working. Many children still use these apps every day. It is very easy to make a new account. Children can just write a false age , or their parents can help them. The big computer companies do not stop the children. Now, the government is angry. They want these companies to pay a lot of money if they do not follow the rules. Other countries are looking at Australia to see what happens next. Difficult words: law (an official rule), government (the people who control a country), age (how old you are). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The technology used in swimming is very advanced, and swimsuits are a key piece of equipment. Designers constantly work on improving swimsuits, and although they might look similar, at the elite level, they are highly engineered and costly. New suit technology often appears at the Olympics, aiming to enhance performance. The sports governing body regulates the materials and design; however, companies still push the limits to create the best suits. Athletes try out different suits to find the best fit. For example, the latest Arena suit includes a new material with compression and flexibility. It takes only two minutes instead of the usual ten to try it on, and athletes feel more buoyant in the water. Testing suits in water with cameras show how they minimize bubbles and help streamline the body. Ultimately, you’ll need to test a few times before deciding on the best suit for race day. Difficult words: elite (the best-trained, best-educated, or richest group in society), engineered (designed and built using scientific principles), buoyant (able to float). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The technology in swimming is very advanced , especially in swimsuits. Designers always try to improve them, making them better for swimmers. The Olympic swimsuits are very expensive and high-tech . The sports body has rules about what materials and designs athletes can use, but companies still try to make the best suits. Athletes test different suits to find the best one. For example, the new Arena suit is easy to put on. It takes only two minutes instead of the usual ten. It makes swimmers feel light in the water. Testing in water shows that the suit helps reduce bubbles and helps athletes swim faster. But you must test a few more times before choosing your suit for the race. Difficult words: advanced (modern and well-developed), designer (a person who creates new things), high-tech (using the most modern methods, designs, machines, and so on). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Swimsuits are very important for swimming. Designers make them better and better. Now, before the Olympics, athletes are looking for the best swimsuits. Olympic swimsuits are very expensive. The sports body makes rules for what materials and designs companies can use. But companies still try to make the best suits. They use new materials. Swimmers test different suits to find the best one. The new Arena suit is easy to put on. You only need two minutes for that. Normally, you would need ten minutes. The suit also makes you feel light in the water. It reduces bubbles, which makes you swim faster. Difficult words: designer (a person who creates new things), body (a group of people who work together and decide on something), reduce (to make smaller or less in amount or size). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
